leg: LANE 3 — Family x5, Europe (AMS/DUB/CDG/LHR) → SFO, Oct 26 or Nov 1-2 2026, lie-flat business (~$16,000 cash equivalent)

options.label: PLAY 1 (WINNER) — Aer Lingus EI61 DUB→SFO, booked with Aer Lingus AerClub Avios, all 5 on one PNR
options.detail: AerClub publishes a FIXED distance chart. DUB–SFO is 4,678 mi = Zone 6 (4,001–5,500 mi). Business off-peak = 62,500 Avios one-way; peak = 75,000. Aer Lingus peak periods are ONLY Christmas/New Year, Easter and Summer — so both Oct 26 and Nov 1-2 2026 are off-peak. 62,500 x 5 = 312,500 Avios. Ireland abolished its Air Travel Tax in 2014 and there is no UK APD, so DUB-origin taxes/carrier charges land roughly $100–165/seat (vs $390/seat on the KLM plan). A330 with true lie-flat business, 5x-7x weekly, and US preclearance at Dublin means the family lands at SFO as a domestic arrival — a real operational win with 3 kids. Amex MR transfers to AerClub 1:1 (near-instant), as does Chase UR; Cap One and Bilt feed it via BA + Combine My Avios.

options.source: https://10xtravel.com/aer-lingus-aerclub-award-charts/ (chart: Zone 6 62,500 off-peak / 75,000 peak business); https://www.headforpoints.com/2026/04/13/2026-and-2027-peak-and-off-peak-avios-flight-dates/ (Aer Lingus peak = Xmas/NY/Easter/Summer only); https://onemileatatime.com/guides/redeem-aer-lingus-avios/ (AerClub cheapest Avios path, low fees); https://www.flightsfrom.com/DUB-SFO (EI61 A330, 5-7x weekly)

Structural argument that decides this lane: a FIXED chart cannot reprice on you. Flying Blue can, and for a party of 5 it will (see PLAY 6). Verify inventory on aerclub.aerlingus.com BEFORE transferring — Amex transfers are irreversible and the ~512k MR figure is a STALE July snapshot.

options.label: PLAY 2 (CHEAPEST IF FUNDABLE) — same Aer Lingus DUB→SFO metal, booked with Alaska/Atmos Rewards
options.detail: Atmos (ex-Mileage Plan) partner chart: business 3,501–5,000 mi = 55,000 points. DUB–SFO at 4,678 mi sits in that band. Fees are ~$26/seat including the $20 partner award fee. 55,000 x 5 = 275,000 points + ~$130 total. That is 37,500 FEWER points and ~$520 less cash than PLAY 1 for the identical seat. Atmos also grants a free stopover, so a few days in Dublin on the way home costs nothing extra. Atmos has an abundance of Aer Lingus transatlantic business space and award alerts routinely show 4 seats open.
options.notes: CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM. The blocker is SOURCING, not pricing. Atmos takes NO transfers from Amex MR, Chase UR, or Citi TY. The only realistic feeders are Bilt (1:1, direct partner) and Marriott (3:1 — you'd need ~660k Marriott points, not realistic). ACTION: verify the Bilt balance first — it is the single highest-leverage unknown in this whole lane. If Bilt holds 275k, this is the best redemption on the entire trip. Also confirm the 4,678 mi routing prices in the 3,501–5,000 band on Alaska's own engine; Alaska's chart is semi-dynamic by partner.

options.label: PLAY 3 (THE REALISTIC EXECUTION) — split 4 + 1 across programs on the SAME Aer Lingus flight
options.detail: Partner feeds (Atmos, BA, United, JetBlue) typically expose a 4-seat cap on Aer Lingus business; AerClub's own site frequently shows MORE inventory than the partner feed. So the practical play is: take 4 seats on whichever partner is cheapest and fundable (Atmos at 55k, or AerClub at 62.5k), then book the 5th directly on AerClub. Mixed example: 4 x 55,000 Atmos (220,000 + ~$104) + 1 x 62,500 AerClub Avios (+ ~$130) = 220,000 Atmos + 62,500 Avios + ~$234. All five on the same aircraft, same day, seated together — just two PNRs.
options.points_cost: 220,000 Atmos + 62,500 Avios (or 250,000 + 62,500 Avios if all-Avios: 4 seats AerClub + 1 seat AerClub, same thing)
options.source: https://awardwallet.com/news/alaska-atmos-rewards/business-class-europe-award-alert/ (4 seats observed); https://10xtravel.com/best-ways-book-aer-lingus-business-class-points-miles/ (partner inventory is often a subset of AerClub's)
options.notes: CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM-HIGH. Answers your question (4) directly: splitting across programs on the SAME METAL is materially easier than splitting across airlines/days, and costs almost nothing extra. Two PNRs on the same flight is a non-issue for seating (call to link) and is far better than the KLM alternative of splitting the family across two different days. Do NOT split across different metal/days unless forced — that is where the real cost lands (extra hotel night, extra positioning, kids on a separate flight).

options.label: PLAY 4 (POSITIONING) — add AMS/CDG→DUB as an award segment, not a separate cash ticket
options.detail: If the family ends in Amsterdam or Paris rather than Dublin, do NOT buy a separate Ryanair/Aer Lingus cash hop — that breaks the protected connection and puts a same-day misconnect on you with 3 kids and transatlantic bags. Instead price AMS–DUB or CDG–DUB as a second segment on the SAME AerClub award: Aer Lingus intra-Europe economy is Zone 2 (651–1,151 mi) = 6,500 Avios off-peak. 5 x 6,500 = 32,500 Avios + ~$25/seat. All-in for PLAY 1 + positioning: ~345,000 Avios + ~$775.
options.source: https://10xtravel.com/aer-lingus-aerclub-award-charts/ (Zone 2 = 6,500 off-peak economy; Avios prices per segment)
options.notes: CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM-HIGH. Note AerClub prices PER SEGMENT, so the two legs price additively — this is not a penalty, it's just how the chart works, and 6,500 Avios for a protected intra-Europe positioning leg is cheap. Even with positioning added, this still beats the KLM plan by ~$1,175 in cash for +45,000 points (2.6 cpp on the marginal points — roughly a wash on pure math, but a decisive win on execution risk). If the family can simply END the Europe leg in Dublin, skip this entirely and PLAY 1 is a clean 10.4 cpp improvement on the margin.

options.label: PLAY 5 (CASH-VS-POINTS BREAKEVEN) — burn the points, do not pay cash
options.detail: Current plan yields ($16,000 − $1,950) / 300,000 = 4.68 cpp. PLAY 1 yields 4.91 cpp; PLAY 2 yields 5.77 cpp. Breakeven math: value MR at a realistic 1.8 cpp hurdle and 300,000 MR = $5,400 opportunity + $1,950 taxes = $7,350, i.e. cash only wins below ~$1,470/seat one-way. At an aggressive 2.2 cpp MR valuation the breakeven is ~$1,710/seat. Market for Europe→SFO business in Oct/Nov shoulder season is ~$2,800–3,200/seat. Cash does not come close.
options.points_cost: n/a — this is the do-nothing baseline
options.cpp: BREAKEVEN = $1,470–$1,710 per seat one-way. Below that, pay cash. Above it, burn points.
options.notes: CONFIDENCE: HIGH on the arithmetic, MEDIUM on the $3,200 cash comp (aggregator data, not live inventory). Verdict: this is a clear POINTS redemption at ~2x-3x the breakeven. One hedge worth pricing: Aer Lingus and KLM both sell economy→business upgrades cheaply (KLM has offloaded seats at $400-700/leg near departure). AerClub's published DUB→SFO upgrade rate is 46,250 Avios off-peak — 5 x 46,250 = 231,250 Avios, but upgrades require an eligible (not cheapest-bucket) paid economy fare and draw on a separate, scarcer upgrade inventory. Treat as a fallback only, not a plan.

options.label: PLAY 6 — CURRENT PLAN (KLM AMS→SFO, 60k Flying Blue x5 = 300k MR + ~$390/seat): KEEP AS FALLBACK, DO NOT LEAD WITH IT
options.detail: The 60,000 figure is a FLOOR on a fully dynamic chart, not a price. Flying Blue's documented behavior for multi-passenger searches: if fewer than 5 saver seats exist on a flight, the engine reprices the ENTIRE party to the flex tier — reported at 142,000+ miles each. That is 710,000 MR for 5 seats, which exceeds the entire ~512k MR pool. Saver business inventory on Flying Blue has been described as 'basically non-existent' on many routes, and the recent bulk saver releases advertised a floor of just TWO business seats per flight. Jarred is Delta Diamond, NOT Flying Blue Platinum/Ultimate — the 2026 enhanced saver-availability benefit is elite-gated and he does not qualify for it.
options.points_cost: 300,000 MR IF five saver seats exist; up to 710,000 MR if they do not
options.cpp: 4.68 cpp at saver; ~2.0 cpp at flex
options.source: https://onemileatatime.com/insights/flying-blue-business-class-award-availability/ (saver business availability collapse); https://onemileatatime.com/news/flying-blue-elite-members-better-award-availability-pricing/ (elite-gated saver access; 60k vs 142k example); https://flightpoints.com/blogs/flying-blue-award-chart-2026-business-class-us-to-europe/
options.notes: CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM-HIGH on the repricing mechanic, HIGH on the elite gate. This is the core adversarial finding: the current plan's 300k number is a BEST CASE that requires an unlikely event (5 saver seats, one flight, one date). It is not wrong to hold it as a fallback — if AwardFares/seats.aero alerts fire showing 5 saver seats on Oct 26 or Nov 1-2, book it. But do not build the trip around it. Search 1 passenger first to find the green calendar date, THEN re-search for 5.

options.label: PLAY 7 — KILLED: fly into LAX or SEA and connect domestically
options.detail: Directly tested per question (1). Flying Blue ELIMINATED the West Coast premium and standardized transatlantic saver pricing for all one-way itineraries regardless of origin or destination — so AMS→SEA, AMS→LAX and AMS→SFO all price identically. There is zero award saving from repositioning, and you would be adding a domestic connection for nothing. On the Aer Lingus side the equivalent trick also fails: DUB–SEA is SUSPENDED from October 25 2026 to April 26 2027, which kills it for both the Oct 26 and Nov 1-2 dates.
options.source: https://thepointsguy.com/news/flying-blue-standardizes-europe-awards (West Coast premium eliminated, standardized pricing); https://travelmole.com/news/aer-lingus-sharp-reductions-for-flights-to-the-united-states-in-winter (DUB–SEA suspended Oct 25 2026 – Apr 26 2027)
options.notes: CONFIDENCE: HIGH. Definitively answers question (1): NO. A related sub-play also fails — DUB→ORD is Zone 5 (50,000 Avios off-peak, saving 62,500 across 5 seats), but the required ORD→SFO domestic leg for 5 costs ~$900 cash or ~75,000 BA Avios, which erases the saving entirely AND adds a connection after an 8-hour flight with three kids. Not worth it.

options.label: PLAY 8 — KILLED: Virgin Atlantic Flying Club for Delta One Europe→SFO
options.detail: The old sweet spot (~47,500–67,500 Virgin points) is destroyed by carrier-imposed surcharges. Virgin now applies the same steep fuel surcharges on Europe→US Delta One as on US→Europe: a documented one-way Delta One award carried 57,500 points PLUS $1,054 in 'taxes and fees,' most of it carrier-imposed. For 5 seats that is over $5,000 in cash on top of the points — worse than paying cash outright on some fares.

options.notes: CONFIDENCE: HIGH. Also disposes of the Delta SkyMiles angle — 132,931 SkyMiles is nowhere near 5 transatlantic business seats regardless. Diamond status buys nothing here.

options.label: PLAY 9 — KILLED: Avianca LifeMiles, and DOWNGRADED: Aeroplan / Star Alliance
options.detail: LifeMiles: the 63,000 transatlantic business rate is GONE. The 2026 devaluation pushed US–Europe partner business to 80,000–92,400 one-way (JFK–FRA on Lufthansa now 92,400), with no advance notice and mixed-cabin pricing eliminated. 5 seats = 400,000–462,000 LifeMiles. Dead. Aeroplan: Europe→North America business at 3,501–6,000 mi = 70,000 points; AMS/LHR/FRA/CDG→SFO all sit in that band, so 350,000 Aeroplan for 5 — more points than PLAY 1, plus Lufthansa/Swiss carrier surcharges, plus ~$250/seat UK APD if routed via LHR. Not competitive.
options.notes: CONFIDENCE: HIGH on LifeMiles (multiple independent 2026 sources on the devaluation), MEDIUM-HIGH on Aeroplan. Neither is worth a transfer. Aeroplan on UNITED metal avoids fuel surcharges and is the only semi-viable Star play, but at 70k x 5 it loses to Avios on both points and taxes.

Iberia Plus books Iberia, BA, Vueling and oneworld partners — and Aer Lingus is NOT a oneworld member (it is an IAG sister airline only). So the Iberia chart is irrelevant here. Silver lining on pooling: Avios is fed by FOUR of Jarred's potential currencies — Amex MR (1:1 direct to AerClub), Chase UR (1:1 direct, both Sapphire Reserves), Capital One (via BA + Combine), and Bilt (direct). summary: VERDICT: the current plan (KLM AMS→SFO, 60k Flying Blue x5 = 300k MR + ~$1,950) is NOT the best play, and its headline number is a best-case that probably will not materialize. Switch to Aer Lingus EI61 DUB→SFO on AerClub Avios: 62,500 x 5 = 312,500 Avios + ~$650 (both Oct 26 and Nov 1-2 2026 are off-peak; Aer Lingus is peak ONLY at Christmas/New Year/Easter/Summer). Nearly the same points, ~$1,300 less cash, and — decisively — a FIXED published chart instead of a dynamic one. THE ADVERSARIAL CORE: Flying Blue reprices the ENTIRE party to flex (reported 142,000+ miles each, i.e. 710k MR for 5) whenever fewer than 5 saver seats exist on a flight, and its recent bulk saver releases guaranteed only TWO business seats. Jarred is Delta Diamond, not Flying Blue Platinum, so he does not get the 2026 elite-gated saver-availability boost. The 300k number requires an unlikely event. Aer Lingus, by contrast, is documented releasing 4+ business seats per flight with the deepest availability in exactly the Sep–Nov shoulder window, and 62,500 is 62,500 no matter how many people search. Add DUB's US preclearance (family lands at SFO as a domestic arrival with three kids) and the case is not close. HIGHEST-LEVERAGE UNKNOWN: the Bilt balance. Alaska/Atmos prices the identical Aer Lingus seat at 55,000 + ~$26 — 275,000 points and $130 total, saving 37,500 points AND ~$520 vs Avios — but Atmos takes no Amex/Chase/Citi transfers, only Bilt (1:1) or Marriott (3:1, unusable at this scale). EXECUTION: expect a 4-seat partner cap, so plan a 4+1 split on the SAME flight (4 on the cheapest fundable program, 5th direct on AerClub, which routinely shows more inventory than partner feeds). If the family ends in AMS/CDG rather than DUB, add the positioning hop as a second AerClub segment (6,500 Avios economy each) rather than a separate cash ticket — protected connection matters here. CASH BREAKEVEN: paying cash only wins below ~$1,470–$1,710/seat one-way; market is ~$2,800–3,200. Burn the points. KILLED THIS PASS: LAX/SEA repositioning (Flying Blue eliminated the West Coast premium — zero saving; and DUB–SEA is suspended Oct 25 2026–Apr 26 2027), Virgin Points for Delta One (57,500 pts PLUS $1,054/seat in surcharges), Avianca LifeMiles (devalued to 80,000–92,400), Aeroplan/Star (350k + surcharges + LHR APD), and Iberia Avios for Aer Lingus (impossible — Aer Lingus is not oneworld; and do NOT route MR through BA, which charges 90,000 for the same seat).
caveats: CONFIDENCE AND VERIFICATION GAPS — read before transferring anything. (1) IRREVERSIBILITY: every transfer here is one-way and final. Confirm live 5-seat inventory on aerclub.aerlingus.com (or Alaska's engine) to the payment page BEFORE moving a single point. AerClub does not offer award holds. (2) STALE POOL: the ~512k Amex MR figure is a July snapshot — re-verify before committing 312,500 of it. Chase UR (Jarred + Ashley Sapphire Reserve + Freedom), Citi TY, Capital One, Bilt, and all hotel balances remain UNVERIFIED; Bilt in particular is the difference between PLAY 1 and the materially better PLAY 2. (3) CHART CURRENCY: the AerClub Zone 6 rate (62,500 off-peak / 75,000 peak) comes from a chart page last dated December 2024 and corroborated by a September 2026 Miami–Dublin datapoint at 62,500 — HIGH confidence but re-price on aerlingus.com before acting. The official 2026 peak/off-peak PDF (aerlingus.com/media/pdfs/AC_calendar_2026.pdf pattern) should be pulled to confirm the exact December boundary; Oct 26 and Nov 1-2 are comfortably clear of it. (4) TAXES ARE ESTIMATED: the ~$100-165/seat DUB-origin figure is inferred from a published $163.30 SFO→DUB datapoint minus US-side taxes, adjusted for Ireland having no departure tax. MEDIUM confidence — could land anywhere in $80–200. (5) SCHEDULE RISK: Aer Lingus is cutting US winter flying and has confirmed DUB–SEA suspension from Oct 25 2026. DUB–SFO is historically year-round and was NOT named in the cuts, but Nov 1-2 falls in the winter schedule — confirm EI61 operates on the specific date before building around it. The Oct 26 date sits one day into winter schedule as well. (6) ALASKA BAND: the 55,000 rate assumes DUB–SFO (4,678 mi) prices in the 3,501–5,000 mi band; Alaska's chart is semi-dynamic by partner, so verify on their engine rather than assuming. (7) CASH COMPS: the ~$3,200/seat figure is from aggregator/deal-site guides, not live inventory — the breakeven conclusion is robust (points win by 2x) but the precise cpp figures shift with the real fare. (8) FLYING BLUE FLEX REPRICING: the 'entire party reprices to flex' mechanic is documented behavior but MEDIUM-HIGH rather than certain confidence; it may be possible to book 2 saver + 3 flex in separate PNRs. Even so, that outcome is strictly worse than a single fixed-price Aer Lingus award. (9) NOT COVERED HERE: this lane addresses only the family of 5. The 3 employees and legs (a)/(b)/(c) are separate optimizations — but note that the Avios pooling breadth identified here (four feeder currencies) may also be the right answer for leg (c) SIN→FCO via Qatar Qsuites, which is bookable with the SAME Avios currency through Qatar Privilege Club.

leg: LANE 4 — Hotel points vs surge cash + optimization of the two already-booked stays (Seoul Sep 27–Oct 6, Singapore Oct 6–10, Rome Oct 9–11, Dubrovnik Oct 18–25, Europe stopover Oct 25–27)
summary: The task's core premise — "award rates CAP the surge (they usually do)" — is FALSE as of 2026 for three of the four chains named. Marriott (charts killed 2022, bounds removed 2023), Hilton (no chart), and IHG (dynamic, old 120k InterContinental cap gone) all price awards dynamically off cash, so they RIDE the F1 surge rather than cap it. World of Hyatt is the ONLY program left with fixed published thresholds, and its Singapore properties (Andaz Singapore, Grand Hyatt Singapore) are Category 6 with a hard ceiling of 40,000 pts/night even on race weekend. That is the entire hotel-points arbitrage on this trip. Second premise-breaker: The Ritz-Carlton Millenia Singapore does not participate in Marriott Bonvoy at all — it cannot be booked on points and earns none, so it is a dead option, not a redemption target. Third: Grand Walkerhill Seoul is an independent SK Networks property on its own in-house Walkerhill Rewards program — not Marriott, not Preferred/I Prefer, not Amex FHR, not The Edit, not Capital One Premier Collection. Points could NOT have beaten $2,160 because no transferable-currency path exists. Do not rebook it for points; there is nothing to rebook into. The adversarial verdict on the two live bookings is mostly DON'T CHURN: the Singapore stay at ~$667/night across Token2049 + F1 Friday is materially BELOW the documented 3-4x Marina Bay race-week surge ($1,000-1,700/night), so the cash booking is already good and the Hyatt swap saves maybe $200-700 of value, not thousands — and only if an unverified Chase UR balance exists to transfer. The two genuinely high-value, un-taken plays are in Europe, not Asia: Hyatt Regency Rome Central (opened Feb 2026, redemptions started at 12,000 pts/night — a Cat 1-4 free-night-cert property in a city where cash runs $300-500) and Hyatt Regency Amsterdam (dropped to Category 4 in the May 2026 reshuffle, now Chase Hyatt free-night-cert eligible). The single highest-priority verification item is not a hotel at all: the claimed 1,378 MQD on the Delta Cars & Stays Seoul booking is internally inconsistent with the claimed 3,449 miles and is at real risk of not posting, because Delta's MQD-on-stays offer is a recurring LIMITED-WINDOW promo (most recent documented booking window June 15 - July 20, 2026) — a stay booked outside a live window earns zero MQDs regardless of travel date.

options.label: HEADLINE ARBITRAGE — Andaz Singapore / Grand Hyatt Singapore on World of Hyatt points (Cat 6, HARD CAP 40,000 pts/night)
options.detail: World of Hyatt is the last major program with fixed published award thresholds — Hyatt explicitly stated in its Feb 2026 announcement that it will keep 'fixed point thresholds rather than moving to dynamic pricing for award nights.' Both Andaz Singapore (Duxton) and Grand Hyatt Singapore (Orchard) remained Category 6 through the May 20, 2026 category reshuffle, pricing 20,000 (Lowest) to 40,000 (Top) pts/night. That 40k ceiling holds even on F1 race weekend, which is exactly the surge-capping behavior Marriott/Hilton/IHG no longer provide. For the Oct 6-10 window (4 nights: Oct 6,7,8,9) that is 80,000 pts best case / 160,000 pts worst case vs the $2,669 already booked. At the 40k Top band: 2,669/160,000 = 1.67 cpp. If it prices at the Moderate band (~30-34k, derived from Hyatt's stated 20-37.5% increase over the old 25k standard): 120,000-136,000 pts = 1.96-2.22 cpp. Hyatt points are consensus-valued 1.7-2.2 cpp, so this is at-or-modestly-above par, NOT a blowout.

The only realistic path is Chase Ultimate Rewards -> Hyatt 1:1 (the single best UR transfer partner), and Chase UR is listed as UNVERIFIED for both Jarred and Ashley's Sapphire Reserve + Freedom. Verify UR balance BEFORE spending any more time here. Also: neither Hyatt property is Marina Bay-adjacent (Andaz is Duxton ~2km from circuit, Grand Hyatt is Orchard), so this is a location DOWNGRADE from the near-MBS booking, which matters if Token2049 at Marina Bay Sands is the actual reason for the trip. Confidence: HIGH on the 40k cap and Cat 6 status; MEDIUM on exact band pricing for the specific dates (Hyatt is rolling Upper/Top bands out gradually in 2026 — 'limited hotels moving a limited number of nights' — so Oct 2026 may still price at or near the old 29k peak).

options.label: PREMISE CORRECTION — Marriott, Hilton, and IHG awards do NOT cap the F1 surge in 2026
options.detail: Marriott discontinued its redemption chart in March 2022 and removed the off-peak/peak minimum-maximum bounds starting 2023; award nights now float with cash rate, season, and demand, and flagship standard rooms that priced 85-100k in 2022-23 routinely clear 120-140k on peak dates with select properties breaching 150k. Hilton Honors has no award chart at all — the published Conrad Singapore Marina Bay 'from 80,000 pts' and Conrad Singapore Orchard 'from 70,000 pts' are FLOOR rates that rise on peak dates, not ceilings. IHG One Rewards is fully dynamic and the former unofficial 120,000-pt cap for non-resort InterContinentals no longer holds, with luxury-tier ranges running 40,000 to 130,000+. Net: on all three programs, the 3-4x race-week cash surge propagates into the points price, so there is no arbitrage to quantify — the redemption gets more expensive in lockstep.
options.cpp: roughly constant across peak/off-peak; no surge protection
options.notes: This directly refutes the lane brief's stated assumption. The only partial blunting mechanisms that survive are structural discounts, not caps: Marriott 5th-night-free on 5+ night award stays (effective 20% off), IHG 4th-night-free for co-brand cardholders (25% off a 4-night stay — and notably the free 4th night can be the most expensive one, so anchoring race Sunday as night four is the right sequencing), and Marriott free-night certs now top-offable with up to 25,000 points as of March 12, 2026 (85k cert + 25k = 110k effective ceiling). None of these is a surge cap. Confidence: HIGH.

options.detail: Two problems. options.label: DELTA STAYS REFUNDABILITY — rate-tier dependent, not brand-level; and disputes route through Expedia, not Delta

Free-cancellation rates typically allow cancel at no cost until 24-72 hours before check-in; prepaid/discounted rates are marked non-refundable and forfeit entirely. Critically, MQDs and miles are NOT awarded for cancelled, no-show, or unpaid reservations — so cancelling to rebook forfeits 100% of the status earn.

options.notes: Rate-neutral but strategically valuable: it preserves ~512k MR for the legs Chase cannot reach (Chase does NOT partner with Emirates, Qatar Privilege Club directly, or Korean Air SKYPASS). ROUTE THE AVIOS THROUGH QATAR PRIVILEGE CLUB rather than booking on BA — Qatar levies NO fuel surcharges (~$30-100 typical cash) while BA carries surcharges on the same award. Add ~$200 for the post-Nov-2025 award seat-selection fee across two sectors. Verify SIN-DOH-FCO schedules given the Feb 2026 Doha airspace disruption.

options.label: LEG D — Virgin Atlantic 50,000/seat, Delta One Europe→SFO (THE OTHER WIN)
options.detail: Chase UR → Virgin Atlantic Flying Club 1:1, near-instant. Virgin devalued nearly everything in its Delta chart but KEPT the old flat pricing for Europe: anywhere in the US to/from anywhere in Europe (ex-UK) is 50,000 points one-way in Delta One. Delta flies AMS-SFO and CDG-SFO nonstop. Delta partner awards carry minimal-to-no carrier surcharges (the ~$1,000 surcharge figure that circulates applies to Virgin's OWN metal, and mostly westbound-origin).
options.cpp: ~6.2 cpp per seat against the ~$3,200/seat cash fare — the highest cpp in the entire plan
options.source: awardtravelfinder.com/how-many-virgin-points-to-fly-delta; onemileatatime.com/guides/redeem-virgin-atlantic-points-delta/ (Europe chart preserved at 50,000 business); upgradedpoints.com (Virgin 1:1 Chase partner)
options.notes: Beats the current KLM 60k Flying Blue plan by 10,000/seat = 50,000 UR saved across five seats, with lower surcharges too. THE CONSTRAINT IS AVAILABILITY, NOT PRICE: five Delta One saver seats on one date is very hard. Plan to split across gateways (AMS + CDG) or across the Oct 26 / Nov 1-2 dates. Delta space is searchable and bookable directly on virginatlantic.com, so you can verify BEFORE transferring — do exactly that, since transfers are final. Chase→Virgin ran a 30% bonus as recently as July 2026; none is live now, but if one returns, 250k Virgin costs only ~192k UR.

options.label: LEG D — Aer Lingus AerClub 62,500/seat off-peak, DUB→SFO business (best availability fallback)
options.detail: Chase UR → Aer Lingus AerClub 1:1, near-instant. Aer Lingus flies DUB-SFO nonstop with a published peak/off-peak chart (not dynamic): the 4,001-5,500 mi band incl. SFO is 75,000 peak, 62,500 off-peak. Late Oct / early Nov should be off-peak. Zero carrier-imposed surcharges — roughly £75 / ~$85-165 one-way. Ireland levies no APD, and Dublin has US preclearance so the family lands domestic in SFO.
options.points_cost: 312,500 Chase UR → Aer Lingus AerClub (5 seats × 62,500 off-peak)
options.source: 10xtravel.com/aer-lingus-aerclub-award-charts/ and onemileatatime.com/guides/redeem-aer-lingus-avios/ (62,500 off-peak / 75,000 peak, ~$163 taxes, no carrier surcharges); headforpoints.com (no APD ex-Dublin)
options.notes: Ties the current KLM 60k plan on cpp but is the pragmatic choice IF five Delta One seats cannot be found — Aer Lingus transatlantic business award inventory is notably deeper than Delta saver. BOOK VIA AERCLUB, NOT BA: the identical award prices 62,500 through Aer Lingus versus 90,000 through British Airways Club — a 27,500-point penalty per seat for using the wrong front door. Do NOT connect through the UK on the same ticket or you eat £172/person in premium-cabin APD.

options.label: LEG D — Flying Blue via Chase (funds the CURRENT plan, no rate change)
options.detail: Chase UR → Air France-KLM Flying Blue 1:1, ~1 hour. Flying Blue IS a Chase transfer partner — worth stating plainly because the brief assumed it might not be. So the existing 60,000 KLM plan can be funded from UR rather than MR at identical cost.
options.source: upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/chase-ultimate-rewards-transfer-partners/ (Flying Blue confirmed Chase partner, 1:1, 1 hour); frequentflyerbonuses.com / loyaltylobby.com Aug 2026 Promo Rewards
options.notes: Rate-neutral source swap. NO HELP FROM PROMO REWARDS: the August 2026 Flying Blue Promo list has only Cayenne, Bogota and Libreville in business — zero transatlantic business routes — and many business promos now require the €379+ Flying Blue Extra subscription. Flying Blue is also dynamically priced, so the 60k quote is date-specific and can move. Virgin at 50k dominates this when Delta space exists.

options.label: LEG D — Aeroplan 75,000/seat Europe→SFO (REJECT)
options.detail: Chase UR → Aeroplan 1:1. Post-June-2026 North America↔Atlantic business for the 4,001-6,000 mi band rose from 70,000 to 75,000; AMS/CDG/LHR/DUB-SFO all fall in that band. Star routing means Lufthansa/SWISS/Austrian/Brussels via a European hub.
options.notes: Listed for completeness and to close it out. Worst of the four leg-D options: most expensive in points, Aeroplan passes Lufthansa-group carrier surcharges (~$400-600/person), it forces a connection rather than a nonstop, and LH group notoriously withholds long-haul business award space from partners until ~15 days out — unworkable for five confirmed seats. Do not use.

options.label: ALL LEGS — Chase Travel portal (Points Boost). The 1.5cpp era is over. (REJECT)
options.detail: The fixed 1.5 cpp Sapphire Reserve portal rate was killed by Points Boost in June 2025 and fully sunset late Oct 2025. Baseline is now 1 cpp on every card, with select bookings boosted to 1.5-2 cpp; CSR tops out at ~2 cpp on eligible premium airfare and select hotels. 2026 reporting shows Points Boost degrading, with some redemptions down to 1.15 cpp, and Feb 2026 saw boosts pull back from premium United fares. Legacy carve-out: cardholders from before June 23 2025 keep 1.5 cpp on points earned before Oct 26 2025, through Oct 26 2027.
options.points_cost: ~200,000-266,000 UR for the $4,000 SFO-ICN fare alone (at 1.5-2.0 cpp)
options.notes: Transfers beat the portal by 3-6x on every leg here — 75,000 points via Aeroplan buys the same seat the portal charges 200,000+ for. ONE legitimate use case: a portal booking is a REVENUE ticket, so it earns Delta MQDs/SkyMiles and elite credit and follows normal fare rules for changes. If Diamond requalification is genuinely at stake, or if award space fails entirely on leg (a), the portal is the graceful fallback — but never the first choice.

options.label: INSURANCE — CSR does NOT cover the 3 employees. Amex Platinum does. (MATERIAL FINDING)
options.detail: Chase Sapphire Reserve trip cancellation/interruption: $10,000 per person / $20,000 per trip, covering the cardholder and IMMEDIATE FAMILY MEMBERS ONLY. Amex Platinum: $10,000 per trip / $20,000 per card per rolling 12 months, covering the cardholder, immediate family, AND other companions traveling on the same trip. For a party of Jarred + family of 5 + 3 employees, CSR's family-only scope leaves the three employees uncovered.
options.source: upgradedpoints.com/credit-cards/reviews/chase-sapphire-reserve/travel-insurance-benefits/ (verified against Chase Guide to Benefits PDF, May 2026); americanexpress.com/us/credit-cards/features-benefits/policies/trip-cancellation-terms.html; squaremouth.com/travel-advice/
options.notes: The offsetting trap runs the other way: Amex requires the ENTIRE trip purchased on the Platinum card, while CSR accepts ALL OR PART — which matters enormously on a cruise where deposit and final payment hit months apart and may land on different cards. Split payment across cards can void the Amex claim outright. Other deltas: CSR emergency medical caps at only $2,500 and has primary rental car to $75,000; Amex has Premium Global Assist evacuation coverage. BOTTOM LINE: neither card is adequate for a $32,000 cruise across 8 people — both cap at $20,000 and CSR excludes the employees. Buy a standalone cruise policy with at least $100,000 emergency medical plus evacuation, and keep the card coverage as a secondary layer.

options.label: PREREQUISITE — Verify balances, then link Jarred + Ashley for household pooling
options.detail: Chase lets you combine UR with ONE other person who shares your address; the link must be set up by PHONE (call the number on the back of either card, give the second account number), after which combining is instant online under Rewards details → Combine points. Freedom cards earn UR but cannot transfer to partners — those points must be moved into a Sapphire account first. Business cards widen this slightly (can also combine with a business co-owner).
options.points_cost: Executing legs a + c + d entirely through Chase needs ~400,000 UR (75k Aeroplan + 75k Avios + 250k Virgin)
options.source: chase.com/personal/credit-cards/education/rewards-benefits/how-to-combine-chase-credit-card-points-in-household; thriftytraveler.com; forbes.com/advisor (one household member, shared address, phone linking required)
options.notes: THIS IS THE GATING ITEM FOR THE ENTIRE LANE — every option above is conditional on UR that has never been counted. Do this first: (1) read Jarred's and Ashley's actual Sapphire Reserve + Freedom balances; (2) call Chase to link the two accounts as household; (3) sweep all Freedom points into a Sapphire account. Only then transfer, and only against confirmed, held award space, because all Chase transfers are FINAL. No Chase airline transfer bonus is live in Aug 2026 — the only active offer is IHG +70% through 8/31, which is not worth taking.

leg: LANE 2 — ALL non-Amex/non-Delta currencies (Citi TY, Capital One, Bilt, Marriott, hotel programs, direct airline balances) applied to legs (a) SMF/SFO→ICN Sep 27, (b) ICN→SIN Oct 6, (c) SIN→FCO Oct 10, (d) Europe→SFO ×5 Oct 26/Nov 1-2, plus Seoul/Singapore/Rome/Dubrovnik hotel nights
summary: HEADLINE: the current plan is probably spending points on the WRONG legs. The single largest cash exposure is leg (d) — family of 5 Europe→SFO at ~$3,200/seat = ~$16,000 — and it has the cleanest, most reliable award solution of the whole trip: Aer Lingus AerClub Avios, DUB→SFO business, 62,500 Avios + ~$163 one-way OFF-PEAK on a PUBLISHED (non-dynamic) chart. 5 seats = 312,500 Avios + ~$815 cash, ~4.9 cpp, and Dublin has US preclearance (huge with 5 people). Avios is a POOLED currency across British Airways Club / Iberia Club / Qatar Privilege Club / Aer Lingus AerClub, and it is fed 1:1 by Chase UR, Amex MR, Capital One, Citi TY, AND Bilt — meaning the existing (unverified) Chase UR + the 512k Amex MR can BOTH fund it. Critically: book through AerClub, not BA — BA charges 90,000 Avios for the identical SFO–DUB seat vs AerClub's 62,500. Second: the same Avios pool solves leg (c) — Qatar Privilege Club Avios, SIN→DOH→FCO Qsuites, est. 65–75k Avios with NO carrier surcharges (Qatar waives them), vs ~$2,600 cash. Third: leg (a) has a genuine sweet spot in Alaska/Atmos Rewards — 75,000 points + $20 for Korean Air Prestige SFO→ICN vs ~$3,900 cash = 5.2 cpp — but Atmos is fed ONLY by Bilt (1:1) and Marriott (3:1 + 5k/60k bonus), and Korean saver space via Atmos is documented as brutally scarce. THREE CORRECTIONS TO LIKELY ASSUMPTIONS: (1) Korean SKYPASS has NO major US transfer partner — Chase and Marriott both ended; you cannot buy KE Prestige with transferable points directly, only via Flying Blue / Delta / Atmos partner awards. (2) Aeroplan's Asia→Europe business went from 87.5k to 102,500 on June 1, 2026 — that sweet spot is dead for leg (c). (3) The Citi→Flying Blue 20% bonus (expires Aug 22) is REAL but is a trap unless you confirm the award first: Flying Blue is fully dynamic (Korean Air business one-ways have been observed 89,000–586,500 miles) and passes through heavy AF/KLM surcharges. HOTEL BOMBSHELL: Singapore Oct 6–10 sits directly on the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix (Oct 9–11, Marina Bay; festival window Oct 2–11). The $2,669 SIN cash booking is F1-surge pricing — historically 2–3x normal, with documented cases of S$1,888/night vs S$500–700 normal. Marriott/Hilton/IHG are dynamic and will surge WITH cash; World of Hyatt is the only major program on a fixed category chart, so Chase UR→Hyatt is the highest-leverage hotel move on this whole trip. Verify Chase UR balances FIRST — Chase is the only currency feeding BOTH Hyatt (1.55–1.6 cpp) and Avios (Aer Lingus/BA/Iberia), making it the most valuable unverified pool in the stack.

options.label: #1 PLAY — Aer Lingus AerClub Avios: DUB→SFO business ×5 (leg d)
options.detail: 62,500 Avios + ~$163 taxes per person one-way, OFF-PEAK, published peak/off-peak chart (NOT dynamic). SFO is Aer Lingus Zone 6. Family of 5 = 312,500 Avios + ~$815 total vs ~$16,000 cash. A330-200 lie-flat business. Dublin has US preclearance — clear immigration in DUB, land domestic at SFO. CRITICAL: book via Aer Lingus AerClub, NOT British Airways — BA prices the identical SFO–DUB seat at 90,000 Avios + ~$159 (27,500 Avios/person worse, ×5 = 137,500 Avios wasted). Aer Lingus imposes no fuel surcharges on Ireland awards. Avios is a shared currency: pool from BA Club / Iberia Club / Qatar Privilege Club / Aer Lingus AerClub via Avios.com. Fed 1:1 by Chase UR, Amex MR, Capital One, Citi TY, Bilt. Awards price PER SEGMENT, so a European feeder into DUB is priced separately (cheap intra-Europe Avios band).
options.notes: CONFIDENCE: HIGH on pricing/chart structure, MEDIUM on 5-seat availability for Oct 26 / Nov 1-2 (must verify live). This reroutes the family through Dublin rather than AMS/CDG/LHR — that is the trade. Off-peak calendar generally covers Oct–Nov, so late Oct / early Nov should price off-peak; CONFIRM the specific date on the AerClub calendar before transferring. Biggest single dollar-saver identified in Lane 2.

options.label: #2 PLAY — Qatar Privilege Club Avios: SIN→DOH→FCO Qsuites (leg c)
options.detail: Est. 65,000–75,000 Avios one-way, taxes ONLY — Qatar waives carrier-imposed surcharges on Avios bookings. Component pricing: DOH–SIN Qsuite business from 50,000 Avios off-peak; DOH–Europe Qsuite business from 42,500 Avios off-peak (Rome is closer than London, so at or below that); connecting through-fares add roughly 15,000 Avios beyond the Doha fare. Free Doha stopover available on select itineraries. Same Avios pool as Play #1 — so the SAME transferred balance can be split across leg (c) and leg (d). Award seats release 355–361 days out; Qatar has been throttling business inventory to non-Avios partners, which makes Privilege Club (and BA) the BEST access channel right now, better than AAdvantage.
options.notes: CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM on the exact Avios number (sources conflict on whether Qatar's chart is distance-based-fixed or dynamic with peak/off-peak ±30–35%); HIGH on the no-surcharge and Avios-pooling facts. MUST price SIN–DOH and DOH–FCO separately on qatarairways.com and compare against the through-itinerary. Use seats.aero Qsuites Finder or Roame (now searches Privilege Club) for space.

options.label: #2b ALT — American AAdvantage 70k for Qsuites (leg c) — Citi TY is the ONLY way in
options.detail: AAdvantage prices Qatar business at a FIXED 70,000 miles one-way to Europe, no fuel surcharges, taxes typically under $50. Citi ThankYou is the only transferable currency that transfers to AAdvantage (1:1, requires Strata Elite / Strata Premier / legacy Prestige — no-annual-fee Citi cards cannot reach airlines). NOTE: Bilt→AAdvantage is DEAD (ended June 2024; AAdvantage is absent from Bilt's official partner list — aggregator sites claiming otherwise are stale).
options.notes: CONFIDENCE: HIGH on the 70k rate and Citi-exclusivity; the WEAKNESS is availability — Qatar has specifically been cutting business inventory released to AAdvantage, and AA's chart doesn't always permit third-region (Asia→Europe) routings without a US connection. Treat Qatar Avios (#2) as primary and this as the fallback. Also verify whether Citi has added Qatar Privilege Club directly — not confirmed in Citi's published partner list.

options.label: #3 PLAY — Alaska/Atmos Rewards 75k: Korean Air Prestige SFO→ICN (leg a)
options.detail: ~75,000 Atmos points + $20 partner booking fee, one-way business, US→South Korea (Asia Pacific partner chart, distance-banded). Vs ~$3,900 KE Prestige cash = 5.2 cpp — the highest cpp of any single-seat redemption found. Korean Air remains a valid Atmos non-alliance partner. One FREE stopover permitted on a one-way partner award (could absorb a Seoul or Asia stopover), but Atmos is single-partner-only — no mixing carriers on one ticket. ACCESS: Atmos is fed by Bilt (1:1, instant) and Marriott Bonvoy (3:1 with the 5,000-mile bonus per 60,000 — so 180,000 Bonvoy → 75,000 Atmos).
options.notes: CONFIDENCE: HIGH on price, LOW-MEDIUM on availability — multiple sources describe Korean saver space via Atmos as 'incredibly difficult, multiple weeks with not a single award seat.' Sep 27 is ~8 weeks out, which is late for KE saver space. This is the ONE case where Marriott's 3:1 airline transfer is genuinely good (2.16 cpp on Bonvoy vs its 0.8 cpp baseline) BECAUSE Bonvoy is one of only two doors into Atmos. Partner fee rose to $20 (from $12.50) July 1, 2026, charged per direction per person.

options.label: #4 PLAY — Chase UR → World of Hyatt for Singapore F1 week (hotels)
options.detail: MAJOR FINDING: Singapore Oct 6–10 collides with the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix, Oct 9–11 at Marina Bay (festival window Oct 2–11; 2026 is a SPRINT weekend, sprint quali Fri Oct 9). The $2,669 SIN cash booking is race-week surge, not a normal rate. Historical surge: rates run 2–3× normal; Fairmont Singapore hit S$1,888/night vs S$500–700 usual; Swissôtel 5D4N ~S$6,460 race week vs ~S$2,075 a week later. Marriott, Hilton and IHG all use DYNAMIC award pricing — their points cost surges in lockstep with cash, so they give you no protection. World of Hyatt is the only major program still on a fixed category chart (8 categories; as of May 20, 2026 the peak/off-peak model was replaced with 5 tiers: Lowest/Low/Moderate/Upper/Top). Andaz Singapore was Cat 6 (~29,000–37,000 pts) pre-change and does not appear on the 2026 category-change lists. Chase UR → Hyatt at 1:1 is the single highest-value transfer available in the entire points stack (Hyatt ~1.55–1.6 cpp vs Marriott 0.8, IHG 0.5–0.6, Hilton 0.35–0.4).
options.notes: CONFIDENCE: HIGH on the F1 date collision and on Hyatt being the only fixed-chart program; MEDIUM on exact Andaz Singapore tier post-May-2026 (must check hyatt.com live). CAVEAT: the new Cat 8 'Top' tier rose 67% (45k→75k) and intra-category spread is now up to 40,000 pts — so 'fixed chart' is weaker than it was. Also: prime SIN properties book 4–6 months ahead for race week and many are pre-blocked by teams/press — award inventory may simply be gone. ADVERSARIAL NOTE: also price the counterfactual of NOT staying in Marina Bay — a non-trackside Hyatt could be a fraction of the cost.

options.label: #5 PLAY — VERIFY CHASE UR FIRST: it is the highest-leverage unknown in the stack
options.detail: Chase Ultimate Rewards (Jarred + Ashley Sapphire Reserve + Freedom, currently UNVERIFIED) is the only currency that simultaneously feeds: World of Hyatt 1:1 (Play #4, best hotel value in existence), British Airways / Iberia / Aer Lingus Avios 1:1 (Plays #1 and #2 — the two biggest cash saves), Air Canada Aeroplan, Virgin Atlantic, Singapore KrisFlyer, Flying Blue, Emirates, IHG and Marriott. Two Sapphire Reserves + Freedom cards can be pooled into one household account. Everything in Lane 2's top 4 plays can be funded from Chase UR alone if the balance is there. LIVE BONUS: Chase → IHG One Rewards at 70% (1:1.7) through Aug 31, 2026 — the largest bonus running this month, though IHG's dynamic pricing means you're arguably 'trading $20 for $8.50.'
options.notes: CONFIDENCE: HIGH that Chase is the right pool to check first. ACTION: log into chase.com/ultimaterewards for both cardholders and report balances before any transfer decision is made. Also re-verify the Amex MR 512k (July snapshot is stale) — Amex feeds BA/Iberia/Aer Lingus Avios 1:1 too, so 512k MR alone could cover the entire 312,500-Avios family leg.

options.label: Citi ThankYou → Flying Blue 20% bonus — CONFIRMED LIVE, expires Aug 22, 2026
options.detail: CONFIRMED: 20% bonus on Citi TY → Air France-KLM Flying Blue, valid for transfers completed 07/19/2026 12:01 AM ET through 08/22/2026 11:59 PM ET. Ratio is 1,200 FB miles per 1,000 TYP with Citi Strata Elite, Strata Premier, Prestige, or AT&T Access More. No-annual-fee Citi cards get only 840 FB per 1,000 (they earn base-level points that cannot reach airlines unless pooled into a premium account). Minimum 1,000 points; transfers process instantly. Effectively cuts award cost ~17%. Standard FB business NA↔Europe starts around 60,000 miles → 50,000 TYP during this promo; stackable with monthly Promo Rewards (25–50% off) for potentially ~38k TYP.
options.cpp: ~5.6 cpp on TYP IF the award and surcharge assumptions hold
options.notes: CONFIDENCE: CERTAIN on the bonus existing and its Aug 22 deadline. ADVERSARIAL WARNING — do NOT transfer speculatively. Flying Blue is FULLY dynamic and passes through heavy AF/KLM carrier surcharges (transatlantic business past $500 CAD each way; AF ex-Europe is worse than KLM ex-AMS). August 2026 Promo Rewards are weak in business — premium economy is this month's sweet spot, business options are limited. Getting FIVE saver business seats on a dynamic program for leg (d) is far less likely than on Aer Lingus's fixed chart. USE ONLY if you find and hold a specific award first. Also relevant: FB can book Korean Air as a SkyTeam partner, but observed KE business one-ways run 89,000 to 586,500 miles with blackout dates.

options.label: Capital One → Avianca LifeMiles 15% bonus (live to Aug 31) — RANKED LOW, devalued
options.detail: Capital One transfers 1:1 to Flying Blue, Turkish Miles&Smiles, Avianca LifeMiles, Air Canada Aeroplan, British Airways, Cathay, Etihad, Finnair, Qantas, QATAR AIRWAYS (1:1 — a direct door into the Avios pool for Plays #1/#2), Singapore KrisFlyer, TAP, Virgin Red. Sub-1:1 partners: EVA (2:1.5), JAL (2:1.5), Emirates (2:1.5), JetBlue (5:3). LIVE: 15% bonus to LifeMiles through Aug 31, 2026 (1:1.15).
options.notes: CONFIDENCE: HIGH. SKIP the LifeMiles bonus — LifeMiles devalued hard: US–Europe business went from ~63k to 90k+ (JFK–FRA on LH now 92,400 one-way), NA–Asia business now 90,000–100,000, and mixed-cabin pricing was eliminated entirely. LifeMiles' only remaining structural edge is zero carrier surcharges (good for LH/Austrian). THE REAL VALUE OF CAPITAL ONE HERE is its 1:1 Qatar Airways line — that is a direct, bonus-free feed into Play #2's Avios pool. Use Cap One for Avios, not for LifeMiles.

options.label: Bilt Rewards — the ONLY non-Marriott door to Alaska/Atmos; AA line is DEAD
options.detail: Bilt (25 partners as of 2026, essentially all 1:1) transfers to: ATMOS REWARDS (Alaska + Hawaiian) — Bilt's key exclusive and the cheapest feed for Play #3; Avianca LifeMiles; United MileagePlus; Flying Blue; Virgin Red; Virgin Atlantic Flying Club; Emirates; BRITISH AIRWAYS, AER LINGUS AERCLUB, IBERIA PLUS and QATAR PRIVILEGE CLUB (four separate doors into the Avios pool — Bilt can fund Plays #1 and #2 directly); Turkish Miles&Smiles; Cathay; Aeroplan; JAL; Etihad; TAP; Southwest; Spirit. Hotels: Hilton, Marriott, WORLD OF HYATT (rare non-Chase Hyatt access — a second door to Play #4), IHG, Wyndham at 1:1; Accor 3:2. Most airline transfers instant; Cathay and JAL same-day.
options.notes: CONFIDENCE: HIGH. CORRECTION TO A COMMON ASSUMPTION: American AAdvantage is NO LONGER a Bilt partner — the partnership ended June 24, 2024 and AAdvantage is absent from Bilt's official list. Any site claiming 'Bilt is the only bank program transferring to AAdvantage at 1:1' is stale/AI-generated. Bilt is uniquely valuable here because it reaches Atmos AND Hyatt AND all four Avios programs. CHECK BILT BALANCE — check Rent Day (1st of month) for a bonus before transferring.

options.label: Marriott Bonvoy 60k→25k airline transfer — good ONLY for Atmos, worthless elsewhere
options.detail: Base ratio 3:1; transferring in 60,000-point blocks yields 25,000 miles instead of 20,000 (effective 3:1.25) via a 5,000-mile bonus per 60k. United is the exception at 10,000 bonus per 60k (60k Bonvoy → 30,000 United, effective 2:1). 39 airline partners, several unavailable from any bank currency. Daily cap 240,000 points transferred (~100,000 miles). NO BONUS on American AAdvantage, Avianca LifeMiles, or Delta SkyMiles. Baseline economics are poor: even valuing resulting miles at 1.5c, Bonvoy nets ~0.4–0.5 cpp — normally a last resort.
options.cpp: 2.16 cpp on Bonvoy (Atmos/Korean case) vs 0.4–0.5 cpp typical
options.notes: CONFIDENCE: HIGH. THE ONE GOOD USE on this trip is Bonvoy → Atmos for Play #3 (Korean Prestige), where 180k Bonvoy buys a $3,880 seat = 2.16 cpp on Bonvoy, ~2.7× its 0.8 cpp baseline — justified purely because Bonvoy is one of only two doors into Atmos. IMPORTANT: Korean Air was REMOVED from the 5,000-mile bonus, and the Marriott→Korean SKYPASS partnership itself is now dead entirely. No Marriott-originated transfer bonus is running as of Aug 2026.

options.label: Korean SKYPASS — CANNOT be fed with points. Structural finding.
options.detail: Korean Air SKYPASS has NO major US credit-card transfer partner: Chase, Amex, Capital One, Citi and Marriott are ALL dead ends. Marriott Bonvoy terminated its SKYPASS transfer partnership (June 2024). The only US card route is the U.S. Bank SKYPASS Visa. Remaining transfer feeds are hotel-only and inefficient: Accor ALL 2:1, Shangri-La Circle 1:1, World of Hyatt 5:2. SKYPASS's own chart is excellent (off-peak business ATL–ICN ~62,500 one-way, occasional 57,500 ORD–ICN; KE First to Seoul 80,000 = the program's sweet spot) — but peak pricing now covers 40% of the calendar, and you can't get the miles. Korean also FORBIDS booking awards for non-family; only registered legal family members can pool.
options.notes: CONFIDENCE: HIGH. This is a load-bearing correction — if the current plan assumes KE Prestige can be bought with transferable points, it cannot. The only points routes onto Korean metal are: Alaska/Atmos 75k (Play #3, via Bilt/Marriott), Flying Blue SkyTeam partner award (dynamic, 89k–586k observed, blackouts), or Delta SkyMiles. The employee-seat angle also breaks on Korean's family-only award rule — SKYPASS awards cannot be issued to the 3 employees even if miles existed.

options.label: Aeroplan Asia→Europe (leg c) — DEVALUED June 1, 2026, do not plan around 87.5k
options.detail: Air Canada Aeroplan's June 1, 2026 chart change hit the Atlantic↔Pacific (Europe↔Asia) zone pair hardest of any pair — 10 of 12 cells increased. Partner business 7,501–11,000 miles rose from 87,500 to 102,500 points (+17.1%). Air Canada / select-partner business 7,001+ miles jumped 67%, from 60,000 to 100,000. The old 87,500 band was the classic SIN/Asia→Europe sweet spot for ANA, Singapore Airlines, EVA and Asiana — it is gone. Applies to all tickets booked or reissued on or after June 1, 2026. Aeroplan is fed by Chase, Amex, Capital One, Bilt, Marriott.

Zones 11–13 rose 5% effective Nov 1, 2025; a further Access-rate devaluation hit Mar 28, 2026. Workarounds: Istanbul (Zone 10) is a sweet spot at ~68,000 business — fly SIN→IST on Saver and connect to FCO on a cheap intra-EU carrier; or watch Spontaneous Escapes (30% off Saver, bookable ~1 month ahead for the following month — Sep bookings would cover Oct travel). Round-trip Saver includes a free 30-day stopover; one-way Saver does not. Turkish Miles&Smiles' famous flat 45,000-to-Europe figure is from 2023 and should NOT be assumed current — Turkish has moved toward dynamic pricing.

KrisFlyer at 108,500 for a $2,600 seat is 2.4 cpp — clearly inferior to Qatar Avios at ~70k with no surcharges. options.label: Virgin Atlantic Flying Club on Delta One (leg a) — degraded, and ICN is offline-only
options.detail: Virgin runs THREE Delta charts: US–UK, US–Europe(non-UK), and a distance-based chart for everything else (incl. Asia) with no peak/standard seasons. STRUCTURAL ADVANTAGE: Virgin imposes carrier-imposed surcharges only on US–Europe/UK travel — Delta awards to ASIA carry NO fuel surcharges. But the famous 60,000-mile US→Asia Delta One rate was destroyed in early 2021; current long-haul bands run materially higher (85,000 covers the 5,001–6,000 mile band on the SkyTeam partner chart; SFO–ICN is ~5,650 mi). Virgin is fed 1:1 by Amex, Bilt, Capital One, Chase AND Citi, and frequently runs transfer bonuses upwards of 35%.

TWO OPERATIONAL BLOCKERS: (1) Seoul/ICN has historically NOT been bookable on virginatlantic.com — requires phoning a Flying Club agent; (2) Delta rarely releases long-haul saver business space. ACTION IF PURSUED: get the Delta distance chart image directly from Virgin's partner redemption page, then phone to price SFO–ICN. Do not transfer first. Adversarial note on the 132,931 verified Delta SkyMiles: Delta's own dynamic pricing to Seoul frequently exceeds 200,000 one-way in Delta One — that balance likely buys ONE seat at a mediocre rate, so do not anchor the plan on it.

options.label: Hotel points by city — where points crush cash vs where cash wins
options.detail: SINGAPORE (Oct 6–10, F1 race week Oct 9–11): points CRUSH cash — see Play #4. Hyatt (Andaz Singapore, The Standard Singapore which DROPPED Cat 5→Cat 4 in May 2026 and is now free-night-cert eligible) are the fixed-chart plays. IHG's Regent Singapore is a documented luxury sweet spot beating IHG's 0.5–0.6c average, and the IHG Premier card's 4th-night-free adds a further 25% off. SEOUL: points LOSE — Seoul is a soft luxury cash market. Josun Palace (Luxury Collection) prices ~$360 cash vs 65,000 Bonvoy = ~0.55 cpp, below Bonvoy's 0.8c baseline. Grand Hyatt Seoul ~$223–245/night cash needs to price under ~28,000 Hyatt points to be worth it. RECOMMENDATION: pay CASH in Seoul, keep the $2,160 Walkerhill booking, spend points in Singapore. DUBROVNIK: Hilton Imperial Dubrovnik (149 rooms, 1 min from Old Town) runs ~70,000 Honors points/night high season, as low as 25,000 off-season; Oct 2026 is shoulder — expect 50,000–70,000. Hilton's 5th-night-free applies on 5+ night award stays. Sheraton Dubrovnik Riviera is the classic target for a Marriott 35,000-point Free Night Award (but it's a 15-min drive from Old Town). ROME: use Marriott's 'Stay for 5, Pay for 4' on 5+ night redemptions; Free Night Awards can now be topped up with up to 25,000 points (raised from 15,000) to reach higher categories.

options.notes: CONFIDENCE: HIGH on the directional call (spend points in Singapore, cash in Seoul); MEDIUM on specific point costs — all of Marriott/Hilton/IHG are dynamic and Oct 2026 rates are not locked. On the refundability question you asked: standard AWARD bookings at Marriott, Hilton, Hyatt and IHG are generally cancellable and re-bookable (points redeposit free) on flexible-rate awards, whereas prepaid/advance-purchase CASH rates typically are not — so a points booking is the strictly more OPTIONAL-VALUE instrument for a trip with this much date uncertainty. VERIFY the specific rate rules at booking; Marriott has been tightening award cancellation windows.

caveats: CONFIDENCE AND VERIFICATION CAVEATS — read before acting. (1) NOTHING HERE IS A LIVE AVAILABILITY CHECK. Every figure is a published-chart or reported rate from Aug 2026 secondary sources; none of it confirms a seat exists on your dates. Transfers are IRREVERSIBLE — confirm and hold the specific award before moving a single point. This applies with maximum force to the two plays I ranked #1 and #3, both of which have documented availability problems. (2) THE FIVE-SEAT PROBLEM IS THE REAL CONSTRAINT ON LEG (d), not price. Finding 5 saver business seats on one flight is the hard part; that is precisely why I ranked the FIXED-chart Aer Lingus play above the dynamic Flying Blue play despite the live Citi bonus. Realistic fallback: split the family across two dates or two carriers. (3) BALANCES ARE UNVERIFIED. Chase UR, Citi TY, Capital One, Bilt, all hotel balances, and every direct airline balance (Alaska/Atmos, United, Virgin, Flying Blue, KrisFlyer) are unknown; the Amex MR 512k is a stale July snapshot. Every play above is contingent on a balance nobody has confirmed. Verify Chase first (it feeds Hyatt AND Avios), then Bilt (only non-Marriott door to Atmos), then Amex. (4) THE 3 EMPLOYEES may create award-booking friction — Korean SKYPASS explicitly forbids booking awards for non-family (registered legal family only), and several programs restrict redemptions to household members. Confirm each program's third-party-booking rule before assuming employee seats can be covered on points. (5) DATA QUALITY FLAGS: Virgin Atlantic's Delta distance chart is published only as an image and I could not retrieve the Asia business figures — the 85,000 cited is from the SkyTeam partner chart and may not apply. Turkish Miles&Smiles pricing is based on 2023-era sources and is likely stale. Qatar's Avios pricing for SIN–FCO is an estimate assembled from component legs, not a quoted through-fare. Andaz Singapore's post-May-2026 Hyatt tier is inferred from absence-from-the-change-list, not confirmed. Aeroplan's SIN–FCO distance band was not confirmed. (6) TIME-BOXED ITEMS: Citi→Flying Blue 20% ends Aug 22, 2026; Cathay 10% ends Aug 28; Chase→IHG 70% and Cap One→LifeMiles 15% end Aug 31. Only the Citi/Flying Blue one is plausibly relevant, and only if you find the award first. (7) ADVERSARIAL BOTTOM LINE ON THE CURRENT PLAN: leg (b), ICN→SIN KE Prestige at $987 LIVE-QUOTED cash, is a FINE cash buy — roughly 1.6–1.8 cpp against any realistic points price for a 5.5-hour regional business seat. Do not burn scarce points there. The points should be concentrated on leg (d) at ~$16,000 of exposure and leg (a) at ~$3,900/seat, in that order. If Lane 1 is planning to spend Amex MR or SkyMiles on the cheap legs, that is the misallocation to fix.
